mechanics.name: One-Two-Three-Four!
mechanics.currentEffect: While standing and idle, press Active Ability 2 to begin a Performance lasting up to 15 seconds. It empowers Survivors within 16 metres and generates continuous Skill Checks during the Performance. If you complete the Performance, empowered Survivors receive a 90-second effect while Healing or Repairing that increases Skill Check occurrence chance by 20%. Cancelling or completing the Performance starts a 110/100/90-second cooldown by tier.
activation: Press Active Ability 2 when the perk is off cooldown.
Ends/deactivates when: The Performance ends after at most 15 seconds or when cancelled.
Ends/deactivates when: The post-Performance benefit is granted only if the Performance is completed and lasts 90 seconds.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.2.0): Introduced; no later material live balance change located in the official notes checked.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: A completed Performance gives nearby Survivors more frequent Healing and Repair Skill Checks for 90 seconds.
mechanics.cooldown: 110/100/90 seconds after cancelling or completing the Performance.
duration: Empowered area: 16 metres from your location during the Performance.
Skill Check chance bonus: 90 seconds after a completed Performance.
specialInteractions: The 9.2.0 live patch fixed an issue where the effect stacked with other Survivors using One-Two-Three-Four!, so duplicate copies do not stack.

editorial.summary: Perform while idle to empower nearby Survivors; the completed performance can increase basic Skill Check frequency for healing and repair for a long duration.
useCases: Support Hyperfocus or Autodidact-style builds that want more Skill Checks.
Set up a team buff before a long repair or healing phase.
Use the performance Aura to signal your support location to nearby teammates.
counters: The benefit is specialized around Skill Check frequency.
Poor team positioning can waste the nearby empowerment.
pros: Can last well beyond the performance.
cons: Much weaker for teammates whose builds do not care about extra Skill Checks.
analysis: One-Two-Three-Four! ranks this position because it supports a very specific but legitimate class of builds. Hyperfocus and Autodidact both become stronger when more Skill Checks appear, so a perk that manipulates frequency can amplify their ceilings.
The performance mechanic is the opportunity cost. The user must stop what they are doing and spend time setting up the buff rather than repairing, healing, or moving to a rescue.

The effect also depends on nearby team composition. A random teammate running ordinary perks may gain little from extra Skill Checks, while a coordinated Hyperfocus setup can deliberately exploit them.
That narrow synergy keeps the perk in mid-B. It can be valuable in an intentional build, but is not something most loadouts want by default.
editorial.verdict: A specialized Skill Check support perk. One-Two-Three-Four! can make high-ceiling generator and healing builds better, but only after deliberate setup.
